findings: No requirement contract, channel plan, issue snapshot or selector changed.
Base and reference verification don't use Serena or the new setting.
The skip policy and selectors are untouched.

Serena's project is created for the configured target_language, java by default, so Symphony setups run the same command as before. Setup fails when indexing didn't install that language's server, so a Serena child can't start a solve whose language server would need a network fetch (CFG-016). Only the target language's server cache is reused or published, in the existing per-version layout.
checks.residual_uncertainty: Checked outside Codex: Serena 1.6.1 created and indexed an Actual Budget checkout for TypeScript in 11 s (1363 files) and installed TypeScriptLanguageServer/ts-lsp. No Serena child ran a solve.

findings: target_language is a progress fingerprint input for setup, indexing, smoke and solve, so timing history doesn't mix languages. Existing history for those stages starts over once because the context now always carries the language.

limitations: This is implementing-agent self-review, not independent semantic review.

No live Codex solve was run.
